text:
Ryan Leonard is 21, in his second full NHL season, and scoring like a top-six winger on about 14 minutes a night. He has 7 goals and 14 points in 18 games while playing 14.3 minutes a night, and 5 of those points have come on the power play.

The goals are mostly earned. He has 5.1 expected goals (the quality of his chances), so 7 is a little hot, not wildly so, and his chance quality per 60 minutes is up from 0.87 last season to 1.18. His hardest shot, 93 mph, is in the 96th percentile among forwards.

The work is at the other end. Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting more chances with him on the ice last season (bottom 9% of forwards), and Washington's five-on-five share is a little worse with him than without him this season. He also drew a maximum fine from NHL Player Safety for a high stick that cut New Jersey's Cody Glass on Nov. 14, but no suspension. Watch whether his minutes grow as his defense catches up.
headline: Leonard is shooting his way into a bigger role
